title: uPVC Window Repairs
summary: Hinges, handles, locks, seals and sealed units repaired on casement and sliding uPVC windows.
body: uPVC windows are the most common type in London homes and most faults are mechanical rather than structural. Friction hinges wear and let the sash drop, espagnolette locks seize, handles snap and gaskets harden and shrink, letting in draughts and water.

We repair and replace this hardware with like-for-like or compatible parts and re-align the sash so the window closes and locks as it should. Where the sealed unit has misted or cracked we replace the glass while keeping the existing frame.
A uPVC frame itself rarely needs replacing. In most cases a targeted repair restores the window for a fraction of the cost and disruption of a new unit.
faults: Window will not close, lock or open fully
Sash has dropped or catches on the frame
Broken or stiff handle
Draughts or water ingress around the opening
Misted or cracked double-glazed unit
Snapped or worn friction hinges

title: Aluminium Window Repairs
summary: Hardware, gasket and glazing repairs to casement, sliding and tilt and turn aluminium systems.
body: Aluminium windows are found in flats, offices, schools and modern houses throughout London. The frames last for decades, but hinges, rollers, locking gear and gaskets wear with use and the sealed units eventually fail.

We identify the system and source the correct hinges, handles, rollers, shoot bolts and gaskets, including parts for older systems that are no longer in production where a compatible equivalent exists. Sealed units are measured and replaced within the existing frame.
Because many aluminium windows are above ground level or in occupied commercial buildings, we plan access and working hours with you before the visit.
faults: Sliding window stiff or jumping its track
Casement will not stay open or close flush
Broken handle or locking mechanism
Perished gaskets causing draughts or rattles
Condensation between the panes
Loose or damaged beading

title: Wooden Window Repairs
summary: Timber casement repairs including rot treatment, splicing, re-glazing and new ironmongery.
body: Timber windows suit the character of London’s older housing stock and, when maintained, outlast many modern alternatives. Problems usually begin with failed paint or putty that lets water into the joinery, followed by swelling, sticking and localised rot.

We cut out and splice in new timber where rot is confined to sills, lower rails or corners, ease and adjust swollen sashes, re-putty and re-glaze panes, and replace worn stays, fasteners and hinges with appropriate ironmongery.
Full replacement is only recommended where the joinery is beyond economic repair, and we will tell you plainly when that is the case.
faults: Soft or rotten sills and bottom rails
Sashes swollen and sticking in damp weather
Cracked or missing putty and loose glass
Draughts around ill-fitting casements
Broken stays, fasteners or hinges
Flaking finish exposing bare timber

title: Sash Window Repairs
summary: Cords, weights, balances, rattles, draught-proofing and timber repairs for box sash windows.
body: Box sash windows are a defining feature of Georgian, Victorian and Edwardian London. They are also robust, repairable and often painted shut or left rattling for years because owners assume the only option is replacement.

We replace broken sash cords and spiral balances, re-hang sashes, free windows that have been painted or swollen shut, renew parting and staff beads, repair rotten sills and meeting rails, and fit discreet draught-proofing that cuts noise and heat loss without changing the appearance.
Cracked or broken panes are re-glazed with suitable glass, and we can advise on slimline double-glazed units for existing sashes where the frame allows.
faults: Sash will not stay open or slides down
Snapped cords or failed spiral balances
Window painted shut or swollen tight
Rattling sashes and cold draughts
Rotten sill, meeting rail or bottom rail
Cracked or broken single-glazed pane

title: Tilt & Turn Window Repairs
summary: Gearing, hinge and handle faults corrected on uPVC and aluminium tilt and turn units.
body: Tilt and turn windows are common in flats and apartment blocks, where they provide ventilation and safe inward cleaning. Their gearing is more complex than a standard casement, and a fault often shows as a window stuck in both modes at once or a handle that will not move.

We release jammed sashes safely, replace worn gearboxes, scissor stays, corner drives and handles, and re-set the mechanism so the tilt and turn functions operate independently again. Sealed units and gaskets are replaced where required.
Most tilt and turn systems are repairable with the correct parts, and a repair avoids the cost of removing and replacing a large sash from an upper floor.
faults: Sash hanging on one hinge after a mis-operation
Handle stuck or turning without engaging
Window stuck in tilt or turn position
Heavy sash dropping and scraping the frame
Draughts around a sash that no longer seals
Failed sealed unit

title: Double Glazing Repairs
summary: Misted, cracked or failed sealed units replaced within existing uPVC, aluminium and timber frames.
body: Condensation or a cloudy haze between the two panes of a double-glazed window means the edge seal of the sealed unit has failed. The frame is almost always fine, and the correct repair is a new sealed unit rather than a new window.

We measure the unit, confirm the glass specification and spacer size, and fit a replacement that matches the existing window. Toughened, laminated, obscure and low-emissivity glass can all be specified where appropriate.
The same approach applies to cracked or broken double-glazed panes and to units that have slipped within the frame, leaving the window hard to lock.
faults: Misting or water between the panes
Cracked, chipped or broken double-glazed unit
Unit dropped in the frame so the window will not lock
Loose, cracked or missing glazing beads
Cold spots and noise through a failed unit

title: Window Lock & Handle Repairs
summary: Broken handles, seized locks, lost keys and failed espagnolette gearing replaced and adjusted.
body: Window locks and handles take the most use of any part of the window and fail accordingly. A handle that spins freely, a lock that will not throw or a window that locks but does not pull tight usually points to the espagnolette gearbox, the keeps or the handle spindle.

We replace cockspur and espagnolette handles, gearboxes, shoot bolts, keeps and restrictors across uPVC, aluminium and timber windows, including locking handles where security or insurance requirements call for them.
Where keys have been lost we can replace the handle rather than the whole window, and we will advise on child restrictors and egress hinges for upper floors.
faults: Handle spins or has snapped off
Window will not lock or unlock
Lock engages but window does not pull tight
Keys lost for locking handles
Keeps and strikers worn or misaligned

title: Window Hinge Replacement
summary: Friction stays, egress and butt hinges replaced on casements that drop, stick or will not stay open.
body: A window that has dropped on the handle side, scrapes the frame or slams shut in the wind has almost always got worn friction hinges. Replacing them is one of the most effective and economical window repairs there is.

We identify the stack height and hinge length, fit matching friction stays or fire-escape egress hinges, and re-adjust the sash so it closes squarely and compresses the seals. On timber and aluminium windows we also replace butt and projecting hinges.
Replacing hinges in pairs keeps the sash balanced and avoids a repeat visit when the second hinge fails shortly after the first.
faults: Window has dropped and catches on the frame
Sash will not stay open or slams shut
Visible gap at the hinge side when closed
Rusted, bent or snapped hinge arms
Draughts at the top or hinge edge

title: Broken Window Glass Repairs
summary: Cracked, broken and damaged panes replaced in single and double-glazed windows and doors.
body: Broken glass needs dealing with promptly for safety, security and weather protection. We remove the damaged pane, make the opening safe and fit replacement glass of the correct type and thickness.

Single-glazed panes in timber and sash windows are re-puttied or re-beaded; double-glazed units are measured and replaced like for like. Where safety glazing is required by regulation, for example in doors or low-level glazing, we fit toughened or laminated glass.
If a replacement unit has to be manufactured to size we can make the opening secure in the meantime.
faults: Cracked or shattered pane
Chipped glass with a running crack
Broken glazed panel in a door or side light
Damage after a break-in or accident
Glass that no longer meets safety requirements

title: Window Seal Replacement
summary: Perished gaskets, weather seals and draught strips renewed to stop draughts, rattles and leaks.
body: The rubber gaskets and brush or pile seals around a window are what keep the weather out. Over time they shrink, harden and pull away from the corners, leaving draughts, rattles, water staining and higher heating bills.

We replace wedge gaskets, bubble seals, flipper seals and pile strips on uPVC and aluminium windows with the correct profile for the system, and fit discreet draught-proofing to timber casements and sashes.
New seals are often combined with hinge and lock adjustment so the sash compresses the seal evenly all the way round.
faults: Cold draughts around a closed window
Rattling sash in windy weather
Water on the sill or staining below the window
Gasket shrunk back from the corners
Black, cracked or crumbling rubber seals

title: Window Frame Repairs
summary: Damaged, split, rotten or discoloured frames repaired in timber, uPVC and aluminium.
body: Frame damage ranges from a small split at a mitre joint to rot through a timber sill or a uPVC frame that has been forced during a break-in. In most cases the frame can be repaired without disturbing the glazing or the surrounding wall.

Timber is spliced or filled with resin repair systems and re-finished; uPVC is welded, filled and colour-matched; aluminium is straightened, re-sealed and re-fixed. We also re-seal the perimeter where the mastic joint to the brickwork has failed.
A sound frame protects the glazing and hardware, so frame repairs are often the sensible first step before other work.
faults: Split or open mitre joints
Rotten timber frame or sill
Cracked, discoloured or forced uPVC frame
Failed mastic between frame and wall
Frame loose in the opening

title: Commercial Window Repairs
summary: Planned and reactive window and door repairs for offices, retail, schools, surgeries and managed blocks.
body: Commercial buildings depend on windows and doors that work every day, and a fault affects staff, tenants and customers at once. We carry out reactive repairs and planned maintenance for offices, shops, restaurants, schools, healthcare premises and residential blocks managed by agents and management companies.

Work covers aluminium and steel window systems, shopfront glazing, communal entrance doors, fire exit hardware and the locks, closers and hinges that fail with heavy use. We can schedule visits outside trading or office hours where disruption must be kept to a minimum.
Letting agents and property managers receive clear written quotations per property and a single point of contact for the work.
faults: Office windows that will not open or lock
Shopfront or display glazing damage
Communal door closers and locks failing
Fire exit hardware not operating correctly
Programme of repairs across several properties

title: Door Lock & Handle Repairs
summary: Cylinders, multi-point locks, handles and keeps repaired or replaced on uPVC, composite, aluminium and timber doors.
body: Door locks fail gradually. The handle gets stiff, the key needs persuading, the door has to be lifted to lock, and then one day the mechanism will not move at all. Addressing the fault early avoids being locked out or in.

We replace euro cylinders, multi-point gearboxes, handles, letterplates, keeps and night latches, and upgrade cylinders to higher-security standards where appropriate. Mortice locks and rim locks on timber doors are repaired or replaced with suitable equivalents.
Lock and handle work is usually combined with hinge adjustment so the door closes without force and the locking points line up with the keeps.
faults: Door has to be lifted or pushed to lock
Key stiff, turning freely or snapped in the lock
Handle floppy, stiff or not springing back
Multi-point lock jammed
Cylinder or lock needs upgrading after a loss of keys

title: Door Hinge & Mechanism Repairs
summary: Dropped, sticking and misaligned doors corrected with new hinges, adjustments and closer repairs.
body: A door that scrapes the floor, catches on the frame or no longer lines up with its keeps has usually dropped on its hinges. On heavier composite and glazed doors this happens sooner, and on communal entrance doors the closer is often the cause.

We adjust and replace flag, butt and rebate hinges on uPVC, composite, aluminium and timber doors, re-align the slab, replace worn closers and anti-slam devices, and renew seals and thresholds so the door shuts quietly and seals properly.
Patio, bi-fold and French doors are covered too, including rollers, tracks and the shoot bolts that keep secondary leaves secure.
faults: Door dropped and scraping the floor or frame
Door swings open or will not stay shut
Hinges loose, worn or pulled from the frame
Door closer leaking or slamming
Patio or bi-fold door stiff on its track
